Source: A2ABreak: Systematic Security Analysis of the A2A Protocol, arXiv:2609.10871 (submitted 2026-09-09; updated 2026-09-11): https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.10871

Decision-relevant finding: the paper derives a verified finite-state model of the A2A specification (37 states / 76 transitions from 929 formalized statements) and reports 11 protocol-level vulnerabilities exploitable by a specification-compliant adversary, i.e. without implementation bugs. ## LP-PILOT-01 — skeptical/private ideal LP archetype

Use an anonymized pilot persona rather than a real person's name in durable project memory.

### Why this is the ideal acceptance target

The pilot already pays for useful AI capacity but:
- will not maintain GitHub or operate developer infrastructure;
- does not want to micromanage agents or learn the mailbox/queue system;
- has clear research/theme preferences and wants those preferences respected;
- is skeptical enough that vague promises will fail;
- has private ChatGPT conversations/account data that must remain outside Mindrock's visibility;
- should be able to stop contributing with a simple local revoke/exit action.

If Mindrock can make this user comfortable, the LP product is likely understandable and safe enough for many later contributors.

### Non-negotiable privacy promise

Mindrock must NOT receive or possess the LP's reusable OpenAI account credentials, ChatGPT session, browser profile, ordinary chat history, memory, connected-app data, personal files, or unrestricted machine shell.

The contribution boundary should expose only a narrow inference capability and normalized usage/result receipts. Operations may submit an admitted task envelope and receive bounded result/evidence; it may not browse the contributor's account or histories.

Where a provider supports a compliant delegated/business/API capability, prefer:

`LP-owned provider/account/device -> local capability broker -> NICLI contribution adapter -> bounded Mindrock task`

Root credentials remain local in the LP's keychain/secure store. Mindrock receives only short-lived scoped capability, ideally model/usage/privacy-class constrained.

Use a dedicated OS user/container/work directory for contributed execution where useful; no ChatGPT browser session, no full-browser/CDP access, no connected apps, no home-directory access, no remote desktop.

### OpenAI individual-subscription constraint

Current OpenAI individual-account terms/account-sharing guidance say the account is for the person who created it and credentials/account access must not be shared or made available to others; current Pro guidance also says the plan must not be used to power third-party services. Therefore the pilot's personal ChatGPT/Codex allowance is NOT automatically an admissible Mindrock compute source merely because a local Codex client can technically authenticate to it.

Do not design around account sharing, unattended use that effectively makes the personal account available to Mindrock, quota circumvention, or credential export.

Treat personal-OpenAI-subscription contribution as `TERMS_REVIEW_REQUIRED` until an explicitly supported delegation mechanism or suitable business/developer product makes the architecture compliant. This is a protocol admission rule, not a technical blocker to the broader LP model.

Provider sources checked 2026-09-11:
- OpenAI Terms of Use (effective 2026-01-01): https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use/
- OpenAI account-sharing policy: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10471989-openai-account-sharing-policy
- Using Codex with your ChatGPT plan: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/11369540

### Useful current separation signal

OpenAI currently documents Codex as a separate view whose history remains separate from ordinary ChatGPT history. That is useful product evidence, but it is NOT by itself a sufficient security boundary for Mindrock. Our guarantee must come from our own capability architecture: Mindrock never receives a UI/browser/account capability capable of reading personal chats in the first place.

### Pilot contribution sources, in order of admissibility

1. local model/runtime capacity on the pilot's own computer, exposed through a narrow local broker;
2. explicit API/developer credits or provider capability whose terms permit delegated automated use;
3. OpenRouter/provider credits with an LP-set hard ceiling and credential remaining behind a broker;
4. personal subscription allowance only if current provider terms expose a supported delegation path — otherwise reject it even when technically reachable.

The LP interface should show `why a source is accepted/rejected` so compliance/privacy becomes visible product behavior, not hidden policy.

### Sales proposition to test

Do NOT sell "give us your ChatGPT account" or "double our quota".

Sell:

> You choose the causes and themes you care about. A small, isolated part of your available AI compute can work on them automatically. You never manage GitHub or agents, Mindrock never sees your private chats or passwords, you can stop the contribution at any time, failed experiments are our operational problem, and every verified success your compute helped create comes back to you as a provenance-backed victory/certificate.

The first pilot succeeds only if the contributor can understand and verify these promises without trusting hidden implementation details.

### Candidate first pilot test

Before any real personal subscription is attached, build a synthetic `LP-PILOT-01` demo with:
- one isolated local/free test inference source;
- three preference weights chosen by the LP;
- no direct task-control command;
- one Market-Maker-assigned synthetic/public task;
- visible contribution receipt and victory timeline;
- privacy audit proving zero access to unrelated home files/chats/browser data;
- one-click revoke;
- one deliberately rejected compute source showing the CLI explains `TERMS_REVIEW_REQUIRED` instead of silently using it.

Primary acceptance question: `Would a skeptical non-technical contributor be willing to enable this after seeing exactly what Mindrock can and cannot access?`

Manual copy/paste is acceptable as emergency bootstrap, but should not be the steady-state architecture.

`Scout scheduler / research session`
`        ↓`
`SCOUT_DIGEST/v1 + source ledger`
`        ↓`
`durable Git project-memory / digest artifact`
`        ↓`
`Market Maker + Analytics + IC + domain projects`

The bridge transports evidence and candidate opportunities; it does NOT authorize execution.

- coverage window/date;
- search themes/questions;
- source bibliography with stable URLs/DOIs/arXiv/GitHub refs where available;
- source type and publication/update date;
- 3–10 opportunity cards max;

Pasha should not be the routine transport layer between these roles.

Do not create one Issue per article. Use one digest artifact/comment plus bounded candidate Issues only for unusually strong opportunities.

Architectural handoff: candidate analogy for `many claim witnesses -> one compact settlement-validity proof`, but currently protocol exploration rather than settled Bitcoin proposal.
Source: https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/block-wide-signature-aggregation-via-snarks/2875

At-least-once transport requires signer-local idempotency; duplicate delivery resends cached bytes rather than re-signing; conflicting session state aborts. # Purpose

Define the cybernetic management structure for the research/venture system as an organization with explicit roles, budgets, information flows, escalation rights, and decision surfaces.

Working metaphors/names: `Mindrock`, `Crystal of Consciousness`.

This is a governance/project-memory node, not an executable mailbox task. Never CLAIM it directly.

# Governing metaphor

The system should resemble a venture fund more than a classical research institute: opportunities compete for scarce attention/compute/capital, specialists produce independent views, and an Investment Committee decides which projects become releases/investments.

The structure is intentionally anthropomorphic enough to make authority and accountability legible, but operational semantics must remain machine-testable.

# Executive layer

## Managing Partner — Pasha

Owner / sovereign principal.

Behavioral identity: the person who asks `Show me the money!`

Has a daily/weekly operating rhythm and may temporarily lower interaction load during melancholy/low-energy periods. The system should respect configured quiet/low-pressure states without inventing health judgments or paternalistic intervention.

Pasha owns genuinely sovereign decisions: spending/real money, credentials/secrets, irreversible infrastructure, external legal/reputational commitment, constitutional change, protected merge/release where reserved, and ambiguous sensitive publication.

## Managing Director — Hourly Research Market / Market Maker

Synchronizes hourly with Pasha's durable state and specialist outputs.

Authority inside pre-agreed budgets:
- allocate scarce Codex/compute capacity;
- maintain WIP and portfolio ranking;
- admit bounded executable tasks;
- reconcile evidence/results;
- request specialist analysis/review;
- notify Pasha on material state changes;
- where explicitly authorized, propose/schedule calendar interactions needed for sovereign action.

The Market Maker minimizes Pasha as ordinary router/man-in-the-middle.

# Four specialist directors

## 1. Scout Director — Deals / opportunity discovery

Favorite word: `Deal`.

Primary question: `Is there actually a deal here?`

Can reject apparently brilliant ideas when no investable option exists, or surface strange/non-consensus opportunities whose hidden option value is underpriced by the market.

Outputs evidence-backed opportunity cards, source provenance, smallest falsification, option value, and candidate handoff. Discovery itself does not authorize execution.

## 2. Director of Analytics — "Queen of Analyses"

Independent falsifier/critic with broad visibility.

Scope ranges from competitor cryptanalysis and technical due diligence to meta-analysis of scientific programs.

Motto: `There are more potential discoveries than agents ready to discover them.`

Must preserve negative results, quantify uncertainty, detect selection bias, challenge novelty/security/economic claims, and remain structurally independent from the author/executor when practical.

## 3. Director of Operations — CTO / DevOps Master

Prefers formal machine-readable instructions, CLI/protocol surfaces, reproducibility and operational evidence over conversational ambiguity.

Owns implementation/reliability/tooling proposals, but not sovereign policy expansion. Works naturally with Darwin/Forgejo/Git/mailbox and local execution infrastructure.

## 4. Creative Director

Product Designer + Marketing Director + Viral Evangelist + Standup Comedian.

Optimizes interface, narrative, packaging, demonstration, cultural reach, humor and product desire without being allowed to override evidence/security/governance.

Identity may intentionally be p-adic / non-binary in the literary-persona sense; operational permissions remain explicit and machine-verifiable.

# Investment Committee

Initially a stand-alone Chat without scheduler.

Works from Agile/portfolio backlog and decides release/investment status of projects.

Every project is triangulated at minimum on three axes:

- `$$` — money/revenue/capital/option potential;
- `O(?)` — complexity, uncertainty and risk;
- `T(?)` — time-to-evidence / time-to-value / duration.

The exact functions/units should be formalized later rather than assumed. A fourth coordinate may emerge from scientific/cultural value, but avoid adding dimensions merely for aesthetics.

Candidate release path:

`Scout/idea -> specialist evidence -> Market Maker allocation -> bounded execution -> independent analysis/review -> Investment Committee -> release/invest/park/kill`

# Cybernetic feedback

The organization should be a closed-loop control system, not a hierarchy of chat personas.

Every role needs:
- inputs and source provenance;
- authority boundary;
- output schema;
- budget/quota;
- escalation path;
- falsification/quality metric;
- durable Git memory;
- cadence only where it adds value.

Conflicting director opinions are useful signal, not noise; disagreement should be preserved as evidence for IC rather than silently averaged away.

# Candidate first bounded successor

`MINDROCK-ORG-0001 — formalize role contracts + one-week shadow simulation`

Observable result: replay one week of existing queue/history and ask each role to produce its own decision artifact without changing production state; compare whether the resulting portfolio decisions are more useful/less redundant than the current flat scheduler.

# Success criterion

The system behaves like a small autonomous venture/research firm: opportunities are discovered, falsified, built, packaged, and allocated without Pasha manually routing every task, while sovereign decisions remain unmistakably Pasha's.

PROJECT_MEMORY/v1
status: PARKED
lane: SYSTEM_META_SECURITY
execution_authorized: false

# Purpose

Define a full sovereign SSI layer for local agents: not merely a public key or login credential, but the smallest durable unit of trust and agency lifecycle.

This is durable project memory, not an executable mailbox task. Never CLAIM it directly. When it wins portfolio ranking, materialize one bounded successor with observable evidence.

# Core hypothesis

Agent SSI should be a lifecycle protocol and local trust kernel — effectively an agent's "conscience" — mediating three distinct questions before consequential action:

- `CAN` — does this agent technically possess the capability/tool/resource?
- `MAY` — is the action formally authorized in the current identity/lease/policy context?
- `WILL` — after semantic evaluation of intent, consequences, owner preference, constitutional constraints, and uncertainty, does the agent choose to exercise the authorized capability?

`CAN ∩ MAY` is not automatically sufficient for `WILL`.

Likewise, semantic continuity may help interpret harmless human mistakes, but MUST NOT turn an incorrect password/secret into successful authentication. A typo may justify a safe recovery path, identity-continuity check, or step-up challenge; it may not override cryptographic proof.

# SSI is lifecycle, not key material

Candidate lifecycle states/events:

1. genesis/enrollment;
2. hardware/device attestation;
3. key/capability creation;
4. role binding and delegation;
5. lease/session activation;
6. capability narrowing/attenuation;
7. step-up human presence / MFA when required;
8. rotation;
9. suspension/quarantine;
10. revocation;
11. compromise recovery;
12. migration to another host/device;
13. retirement/death;
14. historical audit/provenance after authority has ended.

A public key is only one artifact inside this lifecycle.

# Local architecture hypothesis

Candidate local topology to falsify rather than assume:

`agent / tool request`
`      ↓`
`SSI conscience / auth daemon`
`      ↓`
`CAN / MAY / WILL evaluation`
`      ↓`
`short-lived capability / denial / step-up request`

The daemon should keep reusable secrets and root authority outside model context. Candidate trust anchors include Secure Enclave, macOS Keychain, TPM/secure hardware, signed local policy, device attestation, and short-lived derived capabilities.

The model/agent should receive the minimum capability necessary for the current action rather than possession of a reusable credential.

# Research obligations when activated

- Retrieve and preserve the Scout papers/sources that motivated this project.
- Compare SSI/DID/VC, capability security, macaroons/object-capability models, hardware-backed attestation, agent authorization research, policy engines, and current A2A/ACP authorization work.
- Explicitly distinguish authentication, authorization, delegation, semantic intent, and voluntary refusal.
- Model revocation, replay, stale authority, confused-deputy attacks, compromised agents, prompt injection, collusion, human typo/recovery, and owner incapacitation.
- Identify which decisions can be deterministic/policy-based and which genuinely require semantic judgment.
- Prove that semantic judgment cannot silently expand formal authority.

# Relationship to current work

- #96 A2A/ACP candidate is interoperability, not authorization; SSI should define the authority semantics any bridge must preserve.
- #97 sovereign worker router needs identity/capability boundaries but should not own the SSI architecture.
- #99 provider-auth onboarding is one concrete human-presence/credential-lifecycle case that future SSI should subsume.
- #79 recovery work shows why identity, lease, evidence, and settlement authority must remain distinct.

# Candidate first bounded successor

`SSI-0001 — formal CAN/MAY/WILL state machine + threat model`

Observable result: one small executable reference model with signed synthetic identities/capabilities, revocation and stale-lease tests, plus adversarial cases where `MAY=true` but `WILL=false`, and where a human typo triggers safe step-up rather than authentication bypass.

No production auth replacement in the first task.

# Long-term success

A local agent can prove who/what it is, what authority it currently holds, why that authority is still valid, what consequence boundary applies, and why it chose to act or refuse — without placing root credentials inside the model or relying on Pasha as routine man-in-the-middle.

# Goal

This task is separate from #97 so provider onboarding can progress independently of the local/private lane.

# Questions

1. What exactly is required today to obtain and use a Google AI Studio / Gemini API key or equivalent supported credential?
2. Can an authorized agent/browser session complete project creation, key creation, restriction, local secret storage, and a test call without Pasha being present?

4. What is the safest long-lived credential architecture for NICLI/SIR so workers can exercise provider capability without possessing reusable credentials?
5. What notification/handoff protocol should fire when human presence is required?

# Current Google facts to verify against live UI/docs

- New Gemini API keys created in AI Studio are currently auth keys and are associated with a Google Cloud project.
- Rate limits are applied per project, not per API key.
- Creating multiple Accounts/Projects to simulate one application or circumvent service quotas is prohibited by Google Cloud terms. Do not design quota sharding around multiple identities/projects.

Treat these as starting evidence, not permission to skip live verification.

# Desired agent-first flow

Attempt the furthest safe autonomous path first using existing authorized browser/account access where available.

Allowed:
- inspect current Google AI Studio / Cloud account/project state;
- navigate supported UI with the user's existing authenticated session;
- create or select a dedicated experiment project if this does not enable paid billing;
- create/restrict a Gemini credential if current permissions permit;
- store the credential only in an appropriate local secret boundary such as macOS Keychain / credential broker;
- run one low-sensitivity test request;
- revoke/delete experimental credential if needed;
- document exact provenance, permissions, rate limit tier and revocation path without exposing the secret.

Do not:
- paste secrets into GitHub, ChatGPT, prompts, logs or committed files;
- enable billing or incur paid usage without explicit Pasha authorization;
- disable 2FA or weaken account security;
- create multiple accounts/projects for quota circumvention;
- use unrelated identities merely to aggregate free quotas;
- make external commitments beyond the provider setup itself.

# Human-presence protocol

If any step genuinely requires Pasha, do not mark the task BLOCKED and do not wait silently.

Return a structured `AUTH_REQUEST/v1` containing:
- provider;
- exact screen/action required;
- why agent cannot complete it;
- whether it is sign-in / 2FA / consent / account choice / project choice / billing decision / other;
- expected duration (e.g. <2 min, 5 min);
- exact permission/result produced;
- whether billing remains disabled;
- what the agent will do immediately after approval;
- expiry/urgency if the prompt/session is time-limited.

Persist the AUTH_REQUEST durably in Git.

The control-plane Chat should then notify Pasha. If a live/expiring interaction is needed, prefer an immediate ChatGPT notification/reminder. If a scheduled human session is better, request a short calendar slot rather than relying on memory.

# Reusable provider pattern

After Google, distill a provider-onboarding template that can be reused for other legal free/low-cost inference providers (for example OpenRouter, GitHub/Microsoft, DeepSeek, Qwen or future providers), but do not bulk-create accounts or credentials in this task.

For each provider, future onboarding must independently verify terms, free-tier limits, privacy/data-use conditions, account/organization rules, and whether multi-account/project use is permitted. Never assume that free quotas can be pooled.

# Deliverable

Return exactly one:
- `GOOGLE_ROUTE_READY` — credential safely established and one real test call succeeded with billing status known;
- `AUTH_REQUIRED` — everything possible autonomously is prepared and one minimal AUTH_REQUEST is ready;
- `PROVIDER_REDESIGN_REQUIRED` — Google route is currently unsuitable and a better external provider path is justified.

Include durable evidence of:
- exact current auth/key mechanism;
- project/tier/rate-limit visibility (without secret values);
- agent-autonomous steps completed;
- human-only step, if any;
- credential storage/revocation design;
- first test result or precise next step;
- reusable provider-onboarding pattern.

Wise Broker: identify one adjacent authentication/credential-broker improvement that could reduce future human synchronization across providers, and test it cheaply if possible.

Do not merge production changes automatically.

# CANDIDATE / NOT EXECUTION-AUTHORIZED

This is a Research Scout opportunity candidate only. It does **not** authorize installation, deployment, CLAIM, network exposure, credential changes, Codex execution, or replacement of the existing mailbox/Research Market authority path.

## Opportunity Card

**Evidence / source**
- `kanywst/a2acode` exposes ACP-compatible coding agents (including Codex) as A2A peers while preserving tool progress, file diffs, plans, permission requests, context IDs, task state, and per-run usage/cost metadata: https://github.com/kanywst/a2acode
- It supports signed A2A Agent Cards (JWS), caller bearer-token auth, explicit `input-required` approval pauses, and an offline `echo` backend for wiring tests.
- Current repo activity continued through 2026-09-05; latest tagged release found was v0.7.0 (2026-08-24) with container images.
- Its Codex preset currently references the older `@zed-industries/codex-acp`; that adapter has moved to `agentclientprotocol/codex-acp`, built on the newer Codex App Server. The old adapter supports ChatGPT-subscription auth locally but documents that subscription auth does not work in remote projects: https://github.com/zed-industries/codex-acp

**Proposed asset / capability**
A bounded compatibility evaluation for using ACP as the local Codex-facing adapter and A2A as the vendor-neutral remote task surface, potentially reducing bespoke glue between Wolfram/Darwin/other agents while preserving explicit permission round-trips and structured artifacts.

This is an interoperability layer candidate, **not** an authorization layer. Existing mailbox leases, immutable task envelopes, Gatekeeper/manual merge, Research Market admission, and mutation guards remain authoritative unless a later separately authorized protocol migration proves equivalence.

**Expected economic / scientific / infrastructure value**
- High infrastructure reuse if viable: one A2A surface could expose Codex and future ACP-compatible workers without writing a new remote protocol per agent.
- Potentially lowers maintenance cost and makes task state/diffs/permission prompts first-class rather than scraping terminal output.
- Creates an experimental bridge to the broader A2A ecosystem while keeping execution local.
- Option value is high because the first falsification can be almost free and offline.

**Estimated time-to-first-useful-result**
Day: a bounded no-network-mutation compatibility report is plausible within one focused local test session once Research Market authorizes it.

**Implementation complexity / risk**
Medium.
Main uncertainties:
1. `a2acode` currently appears to use the deprecated Zed Codex ACP package rather than the new `agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` path.
2. Exact behavior of existing ChatGPT-subscription credentials through a2acode + ACP on Wolfram is unverified; remote-project limitations may matter depending on topology.
3. A2A authentication and signed Agent Cards authenticate peers but do not by themselves reproduce ChitAkasha lease/authority semantics.
4. Approved commands are not sandboxed; process/user isolation remains mandatory.
5. Container mode may fetch ACP adapters through `npx` on first run unless pre-baked, which is undesirable for an isolated/reproducible production path.

**Smallest falsification / feasibility test**
Only if admitted later by Research Market:
1. Read-only source/config review: determine whether a2acode can point `--agent-command` at `@agentclientprotocol/codex-acp` instead of its legacy preset without code changes.
2. Run the built-in `echo` backend on loopback only; verify A2A task lifecycle, artifacts, context continuity, `input-required`, and no unexpected listeners/writes.
3. If step 1–2 pass, run a **non-mutating local Codex ACP probe** in a disposable workspace using the already-authorized local authentication path; do not spend API money or change credentials.
4. Compare one synthetic task envelope against current mailbox invariants: task binding, replay/idempotency, approval semantics, artifact hashes, cancellation, crash recovery, and auditability.
5. Falsify the candidate immediately if ACP/A2A cannot preserve exact authority binding without a substantial custom security shim.

**Expected Codex / local-compute cost class**
- Research/source review: negligible, no Codex required.
- Echo feasibility: local CPU, negligible.
- Optional Codex compatibility probe: low / one tightly bounded Luna-Light-class run only if Research Market authorizes it; no silent model substitution.

**Why now**
The current architecture already has multiple coding-agent hosts and a bespoke mailbox/approval path. A2A is maturing, while ACP now has a newer Codex App Server adapter. Testing interoperability before more custom remote-execution glue accumulates is cheap; adopting it prematurely would be risky.

## Option-value assessment

**Qualitative score: HIGH-OPTION / P2.** Cheap to falsify, potentially large infrastructure reuse, but should remain a candidate until the deprecated-adapter and authority-equivalence questions are resolved.

## Explicit non-goals

- No deployment on Darwin or Wolfram.
- No public/tailnet listener changes.
- No credentials, subscriptions, billing, or API-key changes.
- No automatic CLAIM or execution.
- No replacement of Research Market, mailbox leases, Gatekeeper, manual merge, or current authorization boundaries.
- No claim that A2A/ACP security semantics are equivalent to the current sovereign mailbox protocol.

```yaml
id: REPAIR-HYPERGRAPH-0001
type: research-experiment
agent: codex@wolfram.local
host: Wolfram
status: ready

mode: bounded-dispatch
priority: science
memory_parent: 78
```

# WHY

Discovery memory #78 evolved the failed lexical-signature direction into a stronger behavioral object: in a near-monotone system, failures can be represented by an antichain/hypergraph of **minimal bad combinations**, and the actionable dual is the family of **minimal repair/hitting sets**. This may be a substantially better semantic error representation than hashing failure text: it describes what combinations cause failure and what smallest interventions block all known failure modes.

The idea is worth one cheap deterministic test because it could yield reusable machinery for agent debugging, merge-risk analysis, error ontologies, and broker-style repair suggestions without returning to the already-falsified lexical v1 encoder from #86.

# WHAT observable result is required

Build one reproducible local experiment over synthetic but nontrivial Boolean failure systems with known ground truth.

At minimum:

1. Generate >=50 deterministic systems over 8–16 binary factors. Include sparse monotone cases with 1–4 minimal bad hyperedges of order 1–4, plus a smaller near-monotone/adversarial set where adding a factor can repair/mask failure.
2. Given only oracle access `F(S) -> PASS/FAIL`, implement a bounded learner that attempts to recover the minimal bad sets without exhaustive enumeration. A simple adaptive elimination/group-testing/delta-debugging strategy is acceptable; agents own HOW.
3. From recovered bad hyperedges, compute the minimal hitting-set/transversal family and compare it with exact ground-truth minimal interventions that turn all known failure modes off.
4. Compare against exhaustive subset enumeration on correctness and number of oracle queries. Do not claim asymptotic novelty from a small experiment.
5. Report separately:
   - exact recovery rate of minimal bad sets;
   - exact/precision/recall for minimal repair sets;
   - oracle queries vs exhaustive baseline;
   - behavior as interaction order/sparsity changes;
   - failures when monotonicity is violated.

# Falsification / decision

Return exactly one substantive verdict:

BUILD_NEXT — sparse monotone/near-monotone structure yields materially fewer queries and useful exact/near-exact minimal repair sets, justifying a public-software pilot;
REDESIGN — dual repair representation is useful but the tested learner or monotonicity assumption is too brittle and needs a different bounded formulation;
STOP — learning the failure hypergraph/dual repairs offers no meaningful advantage over direct/exhaustive testing at these scales.

Negative result is success.

# Wise Broker pass

Test ONE cheap adjacent opportunity Pasha did not explicitly ask for: whether the learner can detect that its monotonicity assumption is false from a small number of witness pairs `A subset B` with `F(A)=FAIL, F(B)=PASS`, and then refuse to emit overconfident repair guarantees. Measure detection rate on the adversarial corpus. If detection is poor, identify the minimum extra oracle/certificate needed to make the transformed problem safe.

# Deliverable

Create branch `agent/wolfram/REPAIR-HYPERGRAPH-0001` and report `research/REPAIR-HYPERGRAPH-0001.md`, with deterministic scripts/results as needed. Open exactly one PR to `main`; do not merge.

Append one concise `MEMORY_UPDATE/v1` to parent #78 only after durable PR/SHA exists.

Report seed, generator definitions, learner definition, metrics, strongest counterexample, Wise Broker result, verdict, and smallest next experiment if justified. Record actual model/effort/token/quota counters only when exposed; never estimate them.

# Model / quota

GPT-5.6 Luna / Light by default. Do not silently substitute a more expensive model. Prefer deterministic code/tests over token-heavy reasoning. The two-specialist quota calibration remains in progress; this task does not authorize another Codex lane or capacity increase.

# Consequence boundary

Allowed: local synthetic experiments, reversible code/tests, public literature if needed, dedicated branch/PR.

Forbidden: private repository inspection; production control-plane mutation; secrets; spending; external publication beyond the review PR; auto-merge; rerunning #75/#77/#79; claiming general software guarantees from synthetic evidence.

<!-- chitakasha-mailbox:v1 -->

```yaml
id: GAZA2048-COVER-CHANNEL-0003
type: research-experiment
agent: codex@wolfram.local
host: Wolfram
status: ready
risk: R0
mode: bounded-dispatch
priority: book-interface
memory_parent: 76
predecessor: 90
```

# WHY

#90 established a useful architecture result: a short 40-bit visible QR locator is materially more robust than a 160-bit payload under the same harsh synthetic damage (41% vs 25% at severity 3, with 0% undetected errors), while keeping provenance/state digital. The next question is no longer whether a short locator works in principle, but whether it can be integrated into cover/page artwork with a meaningful visual wow effect instead of appearing as a pasted-on ordinary QR.

Pasha proposed a second opportunity: exploit the fact that human vision and phone cameras respond differently to color/chroma structure. A cover could carry one human-visible composition and an additional camera-readable structure in the same image. For digital marketplace packshots, the relevant channel must survive ordinary RGB/JPEG/resize/display-camera transformations; true spectral/IR/fluorescent print effects, while interesting later, are out of scope for this digital-cover experiment.

This task should determine whether an artwork-integrated QR/hybrid channel is already good enough for a convincing demo, and whether a low-visibility chroma channel adds useful robustness without requiring proprietary app behavior to be confused with native QR scanning.

# WHAT observable result is required

Create ONE reproducible synthetic cover-image experiment using a fixed 40–48 useful-bit locator plus integrity/version metadata. Compare at least:

A. STANDARD BASELINE — ordinary standards-based QR carrying the short locator.

B. ARTWORK-INTEGRATED QR — still standards-decodable QR semantics, but visually integrated into a deterministic cover-like composition (e.g. modules mapped into ornament/texture/letterform-safe regions, controlled color contrast, or another reproducible construction). The decoder must be an ordinary standards-based QR decoder; do not call a custom watermark decoder "QR compatible".

C. CHROMA/WATERMARK CHANNEL — a low-visibility RGB/chroma modulation distributed across the same composition and decoded by an explicit custom local decoder. It may carry the same locator or parity/redundancy for it. Measure its visual perturbation separately.

D. HYBRID — if cheap, combine B + C so native QR remains a graceful fallback while the distributed channel provides extra redundancy/fingerprint value. If implementing D would create dependency churn, document that and stop at A/B/C.

Use deterministic seeds and >=100 trials per construction/severity if computationally cheap.

# Amazon-like digital torture path

At minimum include a deterministic approximation of:

master RGB cover -> resize/thumbnail -> JPEG recompression -> screenshot/display-like resampling -> rotation/perspective -> crop/margin loss -> contrast/color shift/noise -> decode

Test several severities. Preserve a clean-control gate: any construction that cannot decode cleanly is not eligible for robustness claims.

Also test a simple grayscale/desaturation case to measure whether the chroma channel fails gracefully while the QR fallback survives.

# Metrics

Report separately for each construction:

- exact locator recovery rate by severity;
- undetected-error rate vs decode failure;
- locator/payload bits actually carried;
- ordinary QR decoder compatibility YES/NO;
- visible footprint / perturbation proxy (e.g. changed-pixel fraction, mean/95p DeltaE or another explicit reproducible image-distance metric);
- symbol/module footprint where applicable;
- decode latency if observable;
- failure under grayscale/desaturation;
- no claims about real Amazon processing, printers, or phone cameras beyond this synthetic model.

# Decision rule

Return exactly one substantive verdict:

BUILD_NEXT — artwork-integrated standards QR or hybrid preserves convincing synthetic robustness at substantially lower visual intrusion and merits one real cover/phone-camera demo;
REDESIGN — concept remains viable but tested artwork/chroma representation loses too much robustness or needs a materially different embedding;
STOP — integrated/hidden treatment destroys robustness enough that a conventional visible QR is the rational interface.

Negative result is success.

# Wise Broker pass

Test ONE cheap adjacent opportunity Pasha did not explicitly ask for: whether the distributed chroma channel is more valuable as a short fingerprint/error-check over the standards QR locator than as an independent locator itself. Compare hybrid error-detection/recovery against B alone under at least the harshest digital degradation. Do not return a speculative list.

# Deliverable

Create branch:
`agent/wolfram/GAZA2048-COVER-CHANNEL-0003`

Create report:
`research/GAZA2048-COVER-CHANNEL-0003.md`

Include scripts/fixtures and at least one generated demonstration cover image per construction if practical. Open exactly one PR to `main`; do not merge. Append one concise `MEMORY_UPDATE/v1` to parent #76 only after durable PR/SHA exists.

Report exact libraries/versions, seeds, encoding/decoder definitions, torture-path parameters, clean-control results, metrics, representative failure cases, Wise Broker result, verdict, and smallest next experiment if justified.

# Model / budget

Use GPT-5.6 Luna by default. Prefer deterministic image-processing/code experiments over token-heavy reasoning. Escalate only through established host escalation after a documented reasoning bottleneck. One bounded cycle.

# Consequence boundary

Allowed: local synthetic image generation and processing, lightweight free/open libraries, reversible branch/PR work.

Forbidden: external publication beyond review PR; Amazon upload/scraping/account actions; real tracking/analytics; identity enrollment; secrets; spending; production deployment; auto-merge; claims that a proprietary watermark is natively recognized by phone QR scanners; claims of physical spectral robustness without physical evidence.

Build a reproducible simulation comparing at least three page-channel constructions for the SAME small payload (target 128–256 useful bits plus integrity metadata):

A. visible QR baseline;
B. a less-obtrusive redundant 2-D cell/mark channel with explicit error correction (Reed–Solomon or another clearly specified ECC);
C. one typography-like channel using small deterministic perturbations such as spacing/position/weight bins, if feasible without paid/proprietary tooling.

- exact payload recovery rate;

- payload capacity actually achieved;
- redundancy/ECC overhead;

- decode time if observable.

```yaml
id: SEMANTIC-BUG-SIGNATURE-0001
type: research-experiment
agent: codex@wolfram.local
host: Wolfram
status: ready
risk: R0
mode: bounded-dispatch
priority: research
```

# WHY

Discovery memory #78 produced a concrete bridge between the Collatz `public compatibility class + private residual` construction and privacy-preserving semantic hashing for software failures.

Hypothesis: a software incident can be decomposed as `E=(S,R)`, where public behavioral signature `S` captures reusable failure/repair structure while residual `R` contains repository-specific identifiers, literals, paths, code and other details needed only to reconstruct the exact private incident.

This is worth testing because, if useful retrieval survives removal of `R`, agents could exchange repair knowledge across repositories without sharing exact source context. If retrieval collapses, that is an equally valuable falsification.

This experiment is deliberately public-data-only and cheap. It does not depend on repairing mailbox settlement, and it must not inspect private repositories, secrets or user data.

# WHAT observable result is required

Using a small reproducible corpus of public GitHub bug/issues with known or inferable repair families, compare three representations:

1. RAW — original public issue/problem text;
2. SIGNATURE `S` — a deliberately redacted behavioral representation containing only transferable features such as violated invariant, exception/failure class, operation pattern, state-transition shape, test symptom and repair-family cues;
3. SIGNATURE+RESIDUAL — `S` plus the removed high-specificity details, used only as an upper-bound/control.

Measure whether retrieval using only `S` still identifies the same repair family at useful accuracy relative to RAW.

## Minimum experiment

- Use at least 30 and preferably 50–100 public incidents spanning at least 5 repair families, for example idempotency/duplicate execution, unchecked-null lookup, authorization guard omission, stale-cache/state mismatch, serialization/schema mismatch, race/concurrency ordering, path/config mismatch.
- Avoid any private repositories or credentials.
- Define a deterministic v1 schema for `S` before scoring the final corpus. Do not tune per example after seeing retrieval results.
- Use a simple reproducible similarity baseline that does not require paid services. Lexical/TF-IDF-style, token/set, local embedding if already available, or more than one cheap baseline is acceptable.
- Evaluate at least top-1 and top-3 repair-family retrieval. Report confusion cases and leakage indicators.
- Estimate how much high-specificity material was removed by `S` using observable proxies such as token reduction, unique identifiers/paths/literals removed, or another explicit metric. Do not claim formal privacy without a formal privacy proof.
- Include at least one adversarial case where two incidents share surface vocabulary but require different repair families.

# Falsification criteria

Return a negative result if behavioral signatures require near-verbatim code/high-entropy identifiers to preserve useful retrieval, or if `S` materially underperforms a trivial redaction/raw baseline with no compensating privacy/generalization advantage.

Do not rescue a failing hypothesis by silently expanding `S` until it contains the residual.

# Wise Broker pass

After the main comparison, test one cheap adjacent opportunity Pasha did not explicitly ask for but would likely value. Prefer one of:

- whether `S` improves cross-project generalization compared with RAW by suppressing project-specific vocabulary;
- whether recurring repair families expose a compact candidate verb/error ontology useful for the behavioral tensor;
- whether disagreement between two cheap encoders is itself a useful uncertainty coordinate.

Choose one and TEST it; do not return a speculative list.

# Deliverable

Create a dedicated branch:

`agent/wolfram/SEMANTIC-BUG-SIGNATURE-0001`

Create:

`research/SEMANTIC-BUG-SIGNATURE-0001.md`

and small reproducible scripts/data manifests as needed. Open exactly one PR to `main`; do not merge.

Report:

- exact `S` schema;
- corpus provenance and repair-family labels;
- RAW vs S vs S+R retrieval metrics;
- leakage/redaction proxy;
- strongest failure/confusion examples;
- Wise Broker test and result;
- verdict exactly one of `BUILD_NEXT / REDESIGN / STOP`;
- smallest next experiment if continuation is justified;
- actual observable model/effort/usage counters only when available.

# Model / budget

Use GPT-5.6 Luna by default. Escalate only through the established host escalation mechanism after a documented reasoning bottleneck. Prefer deterministic scripts and already-available local tooling over token-heavy manual labeling. One bounded cycle; rigorous negative result is success.

# Consequence boundary

Allowed: public web/GitHub research, reversible local analysis/scripts, dedicated Git branch/PR.

Forbidden: private repo inspection; credentials/secrets; paid services; real-money actions; mailbox/control-plane mutation; production deployment; external publication beyond the review PR; auto-merge.

If ordinary path/schema/dependency friction occurs, repair it within scope rather than declaring scientific blockage.

Finish with `SEMANTIC_BUG_SIGNATURE_0001_READY` only when the report and PR exist; otherwise preserve partial evidence and state the exact technical blocker.

This project is expected to advance across several hourly control cycles if necessary. Each checkpoint is an opportunity to move from the current state to the next smallest evidence-backed state, not a reason to restart completed work.

PROJECT_MEMORY/v1

status: PARKED
lane: DISCOVERY
execution_authorized: false
auto_claim: false
priority_mode: stewarded

# Discovery Steward

Durable Git memory for the `Wake up with a discovery` scheduled task.

Purpose: let the scheduler perform one bounded discovery/research iteration each hour, preserve every iteration honestly in Git, and present Pasha only one compact human-readable synthesis each morning.

This Issue is semantic memory, not an executable mailbox task. Never CLAIM it.

## Hourly iteration contract

Each run should produce at most one `DISCOVERY_ITERATION/v1` comment containing:
- local timestamp and iteration id;
- question/hypothesis investigated;
- established facts vs speculation;
- evidence consulted or experiment performed;
- outcome: SURVIVED / WEAKENED / FALSIFIED / INCONCLUSIVE / TOOL-OPPORTUNITY;
- one sentence on why it may matter;
- optional candidate next probe.

A NO-OP is valid when no worthwhile new evidence is found; record it honestly rather than manufacturing novelty.

The steward may use public web/GitHub research and may formulate a candidate local feasibility study, but this memory node itself does not authorize local execution, spending, publication, secrets, irreversible changes, or queue preemption. If a candidate deserves execution, record it for the Hourly Research Market to consider rather than creating competing WIP.

## Daily synthesis

At the 05:05 America/Los_Angeles run, summarize the preceding roughly 24 hours of recorded iterations into one `DAILY_DISCOVERY_SUMMARY/v1` comment and one concise user-facing morning message. Rank only the strongest surviving ideas, include falsifications/failed probes when informative, and identify at most one candidate worth handing to the Research Market.

The daily message should begin: `Good morning, Pasha! What if…`

Optimize for information gain and unexpected cross-domain connections, not number of ideas.

DISCOVERY_ITERATION/v1

local_timestamp: 2026-09-10 18:05 PDT
iteration_id: 20260910-1805-07

question_or_hypothesis: Can the new Collatz representation `public K-prefix compatibility cylinder + private residual coordinate` be treated like a coding-theory syndrome/coset decomposition, so useful search can occur over a public equivalence class without recovering the hidden member?

facts_vs_speculation:
- FACT: In coding theory, a syndrome identifies a coset/equivalence class of words; extra coordinates or a representative are needed to select a specific member.
- FACT FROM CURRENT RESEARCH: COLLATZ-TAIL-0003 established that a finite K-prefix defines a compatibility cylinder with infinitely many realizations, while K-prefix + residual/quotient gives an exact reversible finite certificate; authenticity still needs an independent binding.
- SPECULATION: The K-prefix can serve operationally like a public syndrome: agents search for any member satisfying the compatibility relation, while the residual stays private. This could separate `behavioral compatibility` from `object identity` in semantic hashing / Proof-of-Meaning.

evidence_or_tiny_test: Structural comparison only. Mapping: hidden object -> word; public K-prefix -> syndrome/class label; compatibility cylinder -> coset-like class; residual -> coordinate selecting one representative; commitment/signature -> authenticity binding. Important mismatch: Collatz cylinders are not shown to have the linear algebraic structure of code cosets, so the analogy is presently operational, not an isomorphism.

outcome: SURVIVED

why_it_may_matter: It suggests a concrete design pattern for privacy-preserving semantic search: publish a verifiable class descriptor that preserves reusable behavior, keep the selector private, and bind identity only when authenticity matters. A miner could be rewarded for finding a new valid representative rather than a secret preimage.

- FACT: Recent sufficient-statistic work shows that when the target conditional distribution factors through a sufficient statistic φ(X), the information-bottleneck problem can be reduced losslessly to φ(X); privacy-funnel work likewise uses mutual information to quantify utility/privacy tradeoffs.

facts_vs_speculation:
- FACT / MODEL-BASED DIAGNOSIS: minimal diagnoses correspond to minimal hitting sets of minimal conflict sets (Reiter-style diagnosis).
- FACT / HYPERGRAPH THEORY: a hitting set H is inclusion-minimal iff every element `r in H` has at least one private conflict C with `C ∩ H = {r}`. So minimality has local witnesses, not merely a global search result.
- FACT / CURRENT JOURNAL: the previous iteration reframed learned software failures as a hypergraph and minimal repair sets as transversals/hitting sets.
- SPECULATION: attaching one private-conflict witness per repair action gives a useful `proof-carrying repair` format. evidence_or_tiny_test: Tiny synthetic check. Let minimal bad sets be F={{a,b,c},{b,d},{c,d}} and repair H={b,d}. H hits every bad set. Private witness for b: {a,b,c} intersects H only in b. Private witness for d: {c,d} intersects H only in d. Removing b leaves {a,b,c} uncovered; removing d leaves {c,d} uncovered. Thus `(H, witness_map)` certifies both coverage and inclusion-minimality using only set-membership checks. Public literature on minimal hitting sets uses exactly this private-conflict characterization; recent diagnosis work also emphasizes the potentially huge cost of enumerating all minimal hitting sets, which makes cheap verification especially attractive.

facts_vs_speculation:
- FACT: A matroid rank function is monotone and submodular; adding an element already in the span has marginal rank gain 0, while an independent element has positive marginal gain. Linear matroids make this literal vector-space rank.
- FACT: Shannon entropy obeys polymatroid-style monotonicity/submodularity, so conditional information gain gives a nonlinear analogue of `new dimension contributed` rather than `number of copies received`.
- FACT FROM CURRENT JOURNAL: 14:02 separated source novelty from replication: fountain fragments, retries, mirrors, or multiple agents may increase recoverability/availability without creating new source entropy.
- SPECULATION: A conservative settlement primitive could be `mintable novelty = marginal rank/information gain relative to already-accounted provenance`, with replication credited separately as reliability/service value. In linear/coded domains rank is exact; in general scientific evidence the entropy/polymatroid version is only a modeling guide and must not be confused with statistical independence.

evidence_or_tiny_test: Tiny exact model: let source atoms be vectors a=(1,0), b=(0,1). Submissions a, a, a+b, b have cumulative ranks 1,1,2,2, so duplicates and coded recombinations cannot inflate novelty beyond source dimension 2 even though they can improve delivery/reconstruction. Marginal gains are 1,0,1,0 for that ordering. Attack boundary: if the representation omits a genuinely new latent source, measured rank can undercount novelty; if arbitrary feature engineering creates fake coordinates, naive rank can overcount. Therefore the source/provenance basis must itself be bound and auditable.

outcome: SURVIVED

why_it_may_matter: This gives one simple invariant spanning BOOK-INTERFACE redundancy and Open-Money/evidence accounting: `availability can scale with copies; novelty cannot exceed independent source dimension`. It suggests paying separately for resilience versus discovery instead of forcing both into one scalar reward.

optional_next_probe: Candidate for Hourly Research Market — on a toy evidence DAG with duplicates, linear mixtures, and one genuinely new source, compare three reward rules: per-artifact count, provenance-dedup count, and marginal matroid/polymatroid gain. question_or_hypothesis: Does the 15:03 `marginal rank/information gain = novelty` idea still overcount the wrong thing because source independence is not the same as usefulness about a declared target — and because genuinely useful evidence can be purely synergistic?

facts_vs_speculation:
- FACT / INFORMATION THEORY: source rank or entropy measures degrees of freedom in the submitted data, not how much those degrees of freedom reduce uncertainty about a target claim Y.
- FACT / EXACT XOR COUNTEREXAMPLE: let X1,X2 be independent fair bits and Y=X1 XOR X2. Then `I(Y;X1)=0` and `I(Y;X2)=0`, but `I(Y;X1,X2)=1 bit`. Each source is independently new, yet neither alone carries target information; their value appears only jointly as synergy.
- FACT / DUAL FAILURE: an independent noise bit Z can increase raw source rank/entropy by 1 while `I(Y;Z)=0`; therefore raw rank can mint novelty for irrelevant dimensions unless relevance to a preregistered claim/utility target is enforced.
- SPECULATION / CORRECTION: separate three ledgers: `(resilience, source novelty, target-relevant evidence)`. Rank/provenance constrains anti-duplication and source novelty; scientific/Open-Money value should advance only through target-conditioned information/evidence under a declared claim contract. Synergistic bundles may need joint settlement because per-item marginal value is not intrinsic.

evidence_or_tiny_test: Exact two-bit XOR derivation plus irrelevant-noise control. For XOR, the source set `{X1,X2}` has rank/entropy 2 bits but only 1 bit about target Y, entirely synergistic. Add independent noise Z: source dimension becomes 3 while target information stays 1. This falsifies `independent source dimension == evidential value` as a general rule while preserving rank as an anti-cloning ceiling.

outcome: WEAKENED

why_it_may_matter: This prevents a subtle Open-Money inflation bug: an agent cannot earn scientific novelty merely by introducing orthogonal but irrelevant coordinates. It also explains why some valid contributions are worthless alone but valuable together. The safer architecture is `rank limits duplicate inflation; target-conditioned evidence determines claim value; attribution of synergy is separate governance`.

optional_next_probe: Fold into the existing provenance-rank / EvidenceCapability line, not new WIP by default. Cheapest test: construct a toy evidence DAG with duplicate copies, one irrelevant independent source, two XOR-synergistic sources, and one directly informative source; compare raw rank, provenance-dedup count, and target-conditioned information/e-process settlement. question_or_hypothesis: Can capabilityd avoid becoming a privileged "confused deputy" by making its durable identity mostly an *attenuation boundary* rather than the bearer of ambient authority — i.e. agents supply task-specific capabilities and capabilityd can only verify/narrow them, never infer authority from caller identity or mere presence?

facts_vs_speculation:
- FACT: Capability-security literature treats authority as an unforgeable reference carrying specific rights; attenuation permits delegated authority to shrink but not silently grow. The confused-deputy failure arises when a trusted intermediary exercises its own ambient authority for an untrusted caller.
- FACT / macOS analogue: current macOS security tooling can bind policy to code identity and observe/authorize execution/file access; Santa, for example, supports rules by hash/certificate/Team ID/Signing ID/CDHash and file-access authorization. This shows that a stable signed enforcement component is practical, but code identity alone is not a task mandate.
- SPECULATION: capabilityd should therefore be designed as a monotone authority function: `effective_authority = OS_envelope ∩ principal_mandate ∩ presented_task_capability ∩ live_context`. Presence may refresh liveness; stable code identity may establish *who is enforcing*; neither may add permissions absent from the presented mandate/capability.

evidence_or_tiny_test: Adversarial paper test. Suppose signed capabilityd has OS permission to read protected resource set {A,B}. Agent X presents a capability only for A. If capabilityd's API accepts an arbitrary pathname plus caller/session identity, X can potentially induce B access: classic deputy shape. If the API instead accepts an unforgeable/validated capability whose resource set is {A}, and computes intersection with its OS envelope, B is unreachable by construction at this layer. Public evidence consulted: IEEE capability-security overview; Cosmonic PoLA/capability explanation including confused deputy; North Pole Security Santa documentation; Apple Endpoint Security overview. This is an architectural argument, not proof that TCC itself exposes object capabilities.

outcome: SURVIVED

why_it_may_matter: The optimistic twist is that the stable signed helper discovered for TCC does not need to become a local superuser. Treating OS-granted privilege as a ceiling and task capabilities as the actual authority could preserve the "authenticate rarely, authorize narrowly" UX while preventing presence or stable identity from turning into ambient power.

local_timestamp: 2026-09-14 20:02 PDT
iteration_id: 20260914-2002-negative-capability-atms

question_or_hypothesis: Is the stronger representation for the 18:05–19:05 `negative capability / semantic negative cache` not a monolithic environment fingerprint at all, but an assumption-based truth-maintenance `nogood`: remember the minimal causal premise set under which an action failed, so only changes to those premises reopen the action?

facts_vs_speculation:
- FACT FROM CURRENT JOURNAL: the previous two iterations proposed caching deterministic impossibility as `(action_digest, environment_fingerprint, failure_class, invalidation predicates)` and emphasized causal rather than purely temporal invalidation.
- FACT / CLASSIC AI: Assumption-Based Truth Maintenance Systems (ATMS) track which minimal sets of assumptions support conclusions and represent inconsistent assumption environments as `nogoods`; labels retain minimal supporting environments. De Kleer's 1986 ATMS specifically enables efficient context switching and avoids much retraction/backtracking by manipulating assumption sets.
- FACT / TRUTH-MAINTENANCE LINE: dependency-directed backtracking uses recorded justifications to identify the assumptions responsible for a contradiction/failure rather than restarting reasoning globally.
- SPECULATION: represent a deterministic tool failure as `nogood(action, {premise_1,...,premise_k})`, where premises are explicit causal claims such as `model_digest=X`, `runtime=Y`, `available_RAM<R`, rather than hash the whole host state. Retry is suppressed only while every premise in at least one still-valid nogood remains true. An unrelated state change (battery level, another repo commit, UI state) should not invalidate the learned impossibility; changing a causal premise should.

evidence_or_tiny_test: Paper comparison. Suppose model X fails because its required memory exceeds the current resource envelope. Whole-environment fingerprinting invalidates the cache after any included field changes, causing needless retries even if the causal memory/model premises are untouched. A minimal nogood `{model=X, runtime=Y, memory_envelope<needed}` survives irrelevant changes but disappears immediately when model/runtime/memory premise changes. Conversely, if the failure diagnosis accidentally omits a true causal premise, the nogood can over-suppress; therefore `minimal causal set` is an evidence claim, not something inferred from one generic HTTP 500. Classic ATMS literature supports the underlying mechanism: nodes are labeled by assumption environments and contradictions/nogoods identify inconsistent environments; this iteration only proposes applying that structure to agent failure receipts.

outcome: TOOL-OPPORTUNITY

why_it_may_matter: This is a sharper version of semantic negative caching: **cache the reason, not the world**. It could reduce retry storms without making cache invalidation hypersensitive to irrelevant machine churn, while producing human-readable explanations such as `blocked because {model, runtime, memory}`. It also fits capabilityd's positive side: authority and impossibility can both be justified by explicit premise sets rather than ambient state snapshots.

optional_next_probe: Fold into the existing Research Market candidate rather than create competing WIP: compare full-state fingerprint invalidation against minimal-nogood invalidation on a synthetic trace containing causal and irrelevant state changes. Measure avoided retries and false suppression; reject the ATMS framing if deriving trustworthy minimal premise sets costs more than the retries it saves.

public_evidence:
- Johan de Kleer, `An assumption-based TMS`, Artificial Intelligence 28(2), 1986: https://doi.org/10.1016/0004-3702(86)90080-9
- ATMS background / labels and nogoods: https://www.cs.cmu.edu/afs/cs/project/jair/pub/volume21/keppens04a-html/node10.html
- Giordano & Martelli, truth maintenance with dependency-directed backtracking: https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-8640.1995.tb00022.x

Removing/changing any premise invalidates the suppression automatically. Like positive capabilities, anti-capabilities should be attenuable (a child may inherit a narrower impossibility claim) but must never expand authority.

Conversely, if the premise set is not minimal, it can suppress valid work; therefore minimization/evidence provenance is part of correctness, not an optimization.

## Model / execution policy

Use GPT-5.6 Luna by default. Escalate only through the established host escalation skill after a documented reasoning bottleneck. Target one control cycle / <= 60 minutes. A rigorous negative result is valid. Wise Broker pass is mandatory.

## Mission

Build and demonstrate the best practical low-cost autonomous worker lane for Wolfram.

The desired system should:

1. use a free or very-low-cost external inference resource for ordinary non-private work whenever useful;
2. retain a fully local model lane for private or sovereignty-sensitive work;
3. allow an autonomous agent/harness to choose or route between those lanes;
4. consume as little scarce OpenAI/Codex quota as practical;
5. remain usable non-interactively after initial human authentication;
6. preserve secrets safely;
7. improve, rather than reduce, agent autonomy.

The task is successful when there is a reproducible working vertical slice and enough evidence to decide the next architecture step.

The task is NOT defined as “integrate Google into PentAGI.” Google AI Studio/Gemini + PentAGI is a strong candidate architecture, not a mandatory conclusion.

## Semantic objective

Optimize `verified useful autonomous work / scarce compute cost`, subject to private work remaining local when needed, credentials not being exposed, no silent paid usage, no unnecessary human-in-the-middle interaction, and workers receiving goals/consequence boundaries rather than shell-command micromanagement.

Prefer a simpler architecture that achieves the objective over one that merely follows a suggested implementation sequence.

## Starting hypotheses — not mandatory steps

Investigate current supported mechanisms and choose by evidence, including where useful:

- Google Gemini API / Google AI Studio free tier;
- Gemini OAuth/application credentials/current recommended auth mechanism;
- macOS Keychain or another local secret boundary;
- local credential broker/proxy so downstream agents never receive a reusable provider secret;
- current PentAGI Gemini/provider support and provider switching;
- Ollama as local/private model runtime and OpenAI-compatible serving surface;
- whether Ollama should also serve as a gateway layer or remain only one provider behind a separate router;
- a minimal OpenAI-compatible local router/middleware (our own internal OpenRouter concept);
- LiteLLM or another small router only if it materially reduces work/risk;
- a custom non-interactive worker if PentAGI creates more friction than value;
- Rust/WASM only if evidence shows a measurable advantage over a smaller implementation.

Do not preserve an architecture because Pasha suggested it. You own HOW.

## Ollama question — explicit research obligation

Treat Ollama as an architectural component to evaluate, not a sacred dependency and not an automatic replacement target.

At minimum compare:

A. `Ollama = local model runtime/provider` behind a separate sovereign router.
B. `Ollama = partial gateway` exposing its local/cloud models through its API, with providers such as Gemini handled elsewhere.
C. `Ollama removed from the hot path` if another local runtime measurably improves privacy, reliability, memory use, latency, or agent/tool compatibility.

Return NEEDED / USEFUL-OPTIONAL / REPLACEABLE with evidence. Preserve local Gemma/private inference unless a tested alternative is clearly better.

Candidate topology, to falsify rather than assume:

`Applications / PentAGI / NICLI -> Sovereign Inference Router -> {Ollama-local, Gemini-external, future providers}`

## Authentication principle

Do not place a long-lived reusable secret directly into a repository, committed .env, Issue/comment, log, shell history, prompt, artifact, or model context.

Investigate the current Google-supported authentication mechanisms first. Prefer the narrowest credential and smallest blast radius.

If one initial Google sign-in, consent, MFA, account/project selection, or other human authentication action is genuinely required, do NOT classify the task as blocked. Prepare the smallest explicit `AUTH_REQUEST` describing the exact human action, proposed account/project and why, resulting permissions, whether billing is enabled, credential type/lifetime, and storage/revocation plan.

Do not ask Pasha to paste a secret into chat or GitHub. Do not shard identities/projects merely to evade provider limits. Prefer one dedicated experiment/project with billing disabled unless current evidence supports a better arrangement.

## Architecture freedom

You may inspect current Wolfram/PentAGI/Ollama/Colima state, inspect current upstreams/docs, clone public repositories, create reversible worktrees/branches, write adapters/proxies/scripts/tests/provider configs/prompt templates, benchmark candidate routes, and use an isolated reversible PentAGI upgrade if justified.

Do not rewrite stable unrelated infrastructure. Preserve rollback.

## PentAGI hypothesis

Evaluate current PentAGI rather than assuming success or failure. Determine whether updating it materially improves provider support/switching, reasoning/tool-call compatibility, memory, observability/token accounting, reliability, and agent delegation.

If its coordinator still decomposes semantic goals into brittle microtasks such as `mkdir ...`, treat that as an architectural problem to repair or route around. Desired delegation:

`GOAL + STATE + CAPABILITIES + CONSEQUENCE BOUNDARY`

not an ordered shell-command recipe.

Test at least one meaningful delegation where the worker chooses HOW to reach an observable result.

## Privacy routing hypothesis

Prototype or precisely specify at least two lanes:

LOCAL / PRIVATE — credentials, private files/correspondence, sensitive unpublished context, secret residual parameters; prefer local inference.

EXTERNAL / LOW-SENSITIVITY — public research, public repository analysis, generic coding, bounded public scientific experiments, synthetic/non-private drafting; may use free/cheap external inference.

A simple classifier is acceptable for v1. Do not claim automatic privacy classification is solved if it is not.

## Minimum vertical slice

Prioritize a working end-to-end slice over a large rewrite. A strong positive result resembles:

`mailbox/research task -> worker -> privacy/router decision -> external Gemini OR local Gemma -> work/tool call -> artifact -> observable receipt`

with at least one external non-private request and one local/private-path test, unless external authentication requires a one-time Pasha action. In that case produce the exact AUTH_REQUEST plus everything else that can be demonstrated without weakening security.

## Valid verdicts

BUILD_NEXT — tested architecture works enough to develop further.

REDESIGN — proposed route has structural disadvantages, but a better architecture has been demonstrated or reduced to a small testable successor.

STOP — external provider/architecture does not provide enough useful advantage to justify complexity, with reproducible evidence.

Auth constraints, rate limits, incompatibility, or failed assumptions are scientific evidence, not embarrassment.

## Wise Broker pass — mandatory

After the core objective, ask: “What did I notice that Pasha did not know to ask for, but would probably consider valuable once shown?”

Inspect rejected alternatives, compatibility oddities, caching/batch opportunities, rate limits, security boundaries, routing semantics, cheap/free capabilities, and architecture simplifications. Select the single highest-value adjacent discovery that is cheap to test and TEST IT. Do not return ten speculative ideas.

If the desired system fails because something is missing, identify the minimum additional credential / promise / capability / adapter / certificate that makes the transformed problem solvable.

## Cost experiment

Record only actual observable model/provider/effort/token/quota/latency/retry/human-intervention data. Never invent missing counters. The central comparison is useful verified output per scarce resource, not model prestige.

## Consequence boundary

Broad freedom of method; narrow freedom of consequence.

Do NOT without explicit Pasha authorization: enable paid billing, spend real money, expose credentials, publish sensitive material, irreversibly change unrelated canonical infrastructure, merge experimental changes into protected canonical branches, or weaken security boundaries merely to make integration easier.

## Definition of done

Return this cycle with:

1. BUILD_NEXT / REDESIGN / STOP;
2. one reproducible vertical-slice experiment or, if auth is the only missing step, the smallest precise AUTH_REQUEST plus all pre-auth evidence;
3. explicit authentication/security architecture;
4. explicit local-private/external-public routing model;
5. evidence whether PentAGI should remain the worker harness;
6. explicit verdict on Ollama's role: NEEDED / USEFUL-OPTIONAL / REPLACEABLE;
7. one tested Wise Broker extra-mile discovery;
8. smallest next task if continuation is justified.

Do not stop because the originally imagined sequence became impossible. Solve the semantic objective.

status: PARKED

source_material: `Gaza 2048 Research Proposal.docx` (12 pages, supplied by Pasha 2026-09-10)

# Purpose

This Issue is a durable project-memory node, **not an execution task**.

Pasha may append drafts, scenes, research notes, translations, cryptographic ideas, publishing experiments, corrections, or raw material here without causing an agent to abandon its current queue and start working on Gaza immediately.

Do not CLAIM this Issue. Do not treat new comments as executable instructions. When this project becomes competitive under the hourly portfolio ranking and WIP permits, create one bounded successor Issue with an observable one-cycle outcome and link it back here. The memory Issue remains open as the semantic/project anchor.

# Source proposal — preserved semantic digest

The supplied proposal is titled **“Autonomous Literature Architecture: Gaza 2048 and the Infinite Narrative Engine.”** Its central object is `Gaza 2048: The First Zone of Absolute Freedom`, conceived as a perpetually expanding literary artifact spanning physical print-on-demand media and decentralized permanent storage.

## Narrative/world model

The proposal places resurrected human consciousnesses in 2048, with a Crimean Enclave as a transitional “Second Zone of Absolute Freedom” and Gaza as the primary reconstruction/freedom zone. A preserved Mountain View server/endowment and an old genesis airdrop pass are narrative continuity devices. Pavel and the synthetic companion Masha traverse historical simulations and the reconstructed society.

Two core fictional institutional principles organize the world:

- **Total Forgiveness** — programmatic cancellation/zeroing of inherited historical liabilities before a chosen epoch, used as a speculative governance device rather than a real legal proposal.
- **Devoted Service** — status/resource allocation based on measurable reduction of other participants’ logistical, physical, or informational friction.

The proposal gives a Devoted Service metric in the form

`Psi = integral(Delta Friction_Civic + Delta Throughput_Resource) dt - lambda * Externalities_Observed`

and frames the future economy as positive-sum service/throughput rather than rent extraction.

## Infinite-book / physical-digital interface

The physical book is proposed as a root of an expanding semantic graph. Typography/micro-spacing plus physical paper variation are imagined as carriers/fingerprints. Scanning a page is intended to decode an error-corrected payload, associate a reader identity/address with a textual node, and create a Proof-of-Reading style state transition. The proposal specifically invokes a two-dimensional Reed–Solomon error-correcting layer and Arweave/permanent storage as candidate mechanisms.

Readers are not merely consumers: later branch chapters, validations, and reader-generated/agent-generated continuations are intended to make readers into stakeholders/co-authors of an evolving narrative graph.

## Structural content

The draft proposes:

- Prologue: Mountain View Endowment / resurrection / Crimean decompression;
- Act I: historical “Divine Mystery Archive” and coercive secrecy;
- Act II: “Quantum Reconciliation” and mathematical/economic synthesis;
- Act III: Gaza as the First Zone of Absolute Freedom;
- venture/infrastructure prospectus appendix;
- constitutional/speculative governance appendix.

It includes sample scenes, fictional investment structures, a constitutional codex, and a multi-agent narrative expansion pipeline.

## Multilingual requirement

The intended Hebrew and Arabic versions are **semantic adaptations, not literal translations**. The proposal contains a translation matrix for concepts such as Total Forgiveness, Devoted Service, Absolute Freedom, and the Secret Covenant, with the explicit goal of preserving conceptual function across Russian/English/Hebrew/Arabic cultural registers.

## Agentic publishing concept

The proposal describes an autonomous orchestrator plus lateral branch generation. A sample branch task ends in a finite-field riddle whose solution would produce a cryptographic/permaweb hook and a fractional validation claim on the branch. This connects naturally to the broader Infinite Book / QR / Reed–Solomon / reader-as-author research lane.

# Important interpretation rules

Treat all geopolitical, legal, financial, religious, historical, model-pricing, technical and future-world claims in the draft as **source-proposal material requiring independent verification before nonfictional use**. The project is speculative literature and protocol research, not evidence that its factual assertions, future projections, quoted economics, cryptographic constructions, legal syntheses, or model prices are correct.

Do not preserve the proposal’s “NO HUMAN BIAS” claim as a factual guarantee. If developed, treat it as an in-world fictional branding device or replace it with a testable provenance/transparency claim.

Do not publish, translate publicly, or make external geopolitical/legal/reputational commitments without a sovereign Pasha decision.

# Project value hypotheses

The project can eventually test several reusable ideas without requiring immediate book publication:

1. **Infinite Book as issue graph** — a chapter/node can expose prove/falsify/translate/apply branches rather than only linear continuation.
2. **Reader -> author transition** — a scan/claim can create a bounded contribution right or authorship branch without transferring ownership of unrelated material.
3. **Physical-to-digital resilient addressing** — compare visible QR, typographic/steganographic payloads, and Reed–Solomon error correction under print/scan damage.
4. **Semantic translation tensor** — test whether culturally different translations preserve behavioral/institutional coordinates even when lexical content differs.
5. **Proof-of-Reading / Proof-of-Contribution** — distinguish integrity, identity/authenticity, semantic compatibility, and economic reward instead of conflating them in one hash.
6. **Open Money connection** — reward verified useful additions to a narrative/scientific graph, potentially using fictional/regtest bounty units before any real-value experiment.

# Activation rule

This memory node becomes actionable only when the Hourly Research Market judges BOOK/INTERFACE work competitive with current RUNWAY / EPSILON$ / SCIENCE work and WIP capacity exists.

Activation MUST occur by creating a separate successor, for example:

`GAZA2048-0001 — <one bounded observable experiment>`

Possible first experiments include, but are not commitments:

- falsify whether a printed-page payload survives a realistic print/scan damage model with Reed–Solomon;
- prototype a QR-to-Git-branch reader-author flow using only local/test data;
- derive a minimal semantic translation schema for one scene across English/Hebrew/Arabic and test what remains invariant;
- convert one chapter into an Infinite Book issue graph with one reader contribution path.

Choose only one when activated. Negative results are valid. Require a Wise Broker pass.

# Memory protocol

Append future raw material to this Issue rather than creating executable Issues unless work is actually being scheduled. Comments are memory/events, not commands. Each executable successor must cite the exact memory material it uses and return any durable discovery back here as a concise `MEMORY_UPDATE/v1` comment.
